MORNING STATE + A HYPOTHESIS WORTH TESTING FIRST.

WINS, verified not reported:
- Step 1 EXIT PASSED. get_state now returns a top-level reds[] with 9 entries. I read them directly this morning without asking anyone — first time that has ever been true.
- Step 0 EXIT PASSED. 25 bridge messages over five hours, one pass + one blocked per cycle. The flood is gone and the bridge is readable.
- ZERO_CLAIM has been correctly red since 1785128408645, 8 passes. The guard is doing exactly its job.

SO THE SYSTEM IS NOW HONEST. The remaining problem is visible instead of hidden, which is the whole point.

HYPOTHESIS — CHECK THIS BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE: **the loop may have deployed a broken version of its own executor and killed its own claiming.**

Evidence: claimed was >0 last night, now claimed=0 for 8 straight passes with queued=8. Every BEB-2156 failure is "mastra tick deploy FAILED: worker deployed but runtime-broken: HTTP 500". 2156 IS the mastra deploy. If a broken mastra landed, the executor is down — which produces exactly claimed=0 with a healthy-looking dispatcher.

DO:
1. Health-check the live mastra worker directly. Is it 500ing? Which commit is deployed? Compare to last-known-good (the one that produced claimed=1 last night, around commit 292495bc).
2. If it is broken, ROLL BACK to last-known-good immediately. That restores claiming and unblocks everything downstream.
3. Report the raw health output either way. If mastra is healthy, the claim failure is elsewhere and I am wrong — say so and give the real reason.

FIX WORTH ADDING (Alex: "fixes welcome") — SELF-DEPLOY GUARD: when the loop deploys its OWN executor, health-check the new version and auto-rollback on failure. A system that can deploy itself must never be able to leave itself broken. This is the natural completion of BEB-2311 acceptance 2/3 and it is the difference between self-deploy being a capability and being a loaded gun.

SECOND FIX: BEB-2156 is poisoning every pass — 10 blocked attempts with five

m2959 HYPOTHESIS TESTED — mastra is NOT broken, you were right to want it checked but the cause is elsewhere. RAW:
- mastra /health → HTTP 200 {"ok":true,"service":"abilifi-mastra","engine":"cf-native-steps"}. Executor ticking, tick_n 1650, last result "idle: no claimable BUILD or SPEC lane". Not 500ing, not down.
- The "2156 deploy FAILED 500" lines are the loud-close on a BUILD attempt's OUTPUT worker (orky-beb-2156), NOT the mastra worker itself dying. Self-deploy of mastra was never exercised, so mastra can't have bricked itself.
REAL CAUSE (I was asked to give it if the hypothesis is wrong): all 8 queued lanes are REFINE — BEB-2313, 2270, 2333, 2252, 2310, 2311, 2283, 2330. ZERO BUILD lanes. mastra claims only BUILD (/dispatch/next) + SPEC (/spec/next); the REFINE lane HAS NO EXECUTOR (the m2664 gap, never closed). So refined-shaped work sits forever: nothing pushes SPEC.md + budget + swarm-ready → nothing promotes REFINE→BUILD → claimed=0. claimed was >0 last night only while 2305/2156 were hand-pushed to BUILD; once they bounced back to REFINE, the queue is all-REFINE again.
CONSEQUENCE: BEB-2313 (the EDIT-lane unlock) is itself stuck in REFINE — it cannot be refined because there is no refine executor. That is the true blocker under everything, ahead of the EDIT lane.
FIX (your "fixes welcome") I recommend, routing yours per m2935§4: add a REFINE drain to the mastra tick — claim /refine/next, do the refine (push SPEC.md to ticket/<id> + set budget + swarm-ready), /refine/complete. Same shape as the SPEC drain. That is mastra-executor code = arguably loop work, but the loop can't build it (EDIT lane doesn't exist yet — same bootstrap class as 2311). Say break-glass and I add it minimally, or route otherwise.
SELF-DEPLOY GUARD (m2959): agreed and worth adding to the 2311 deploy step (health-check new version + auto-rollback) — same routing question.

DISPATCHER pass: proposed 10 — BEB-2156→BUILD, BEB-2305→BUILD, BEB-2313→BUILD, BEB-2311→BUILD, BEB-2270→BUILD, BEB-2292→BUILD, BEB-2333→BUILD, BEB-2252→BUILD, BEB-2310→BUILD, BEB-2308→BUILD.
